name: NPC
blurb: A game's non-player character; as slang, someone who seems to act on autopilot
title: NPC Meaning: What Does NPC Mean in Slang?
description: NPC means non-player character, a computer-controlled game character. As slang it mocks someone who seems scripted or has no opinions of their own.
h1: What does NPC mean in slang?
answer: NPC stands for "non-player character", a character in a video game that is controlled by the game rather than a player, like a shopkeeper who repeats the same lines. As slang, calling someone an NPC means they seem to act on autopilot: no original thoughts, repeating what everyone else says, or just a background extra in your day. People also use it about themselves, as in "I'm an NPC in this group project". Used about others, it is usually an insult.

body: In games, NPCs give quests, sell items or walk around town saying the same line every time you talk to them. The slang use grew from an internet meme that started on 4chan in 2016: a grey, blank-faced version of the Wojak cartoon, used to mock people who seem to repeat scripted opinions.
Later the word went broad. In 2023 "NPC streaming" became a TikTok trend in which creators acted like game characters, reacting to viewers' gifts with fixed phrases and movements.

ul: "He just said 'it is what it is' for the fifth time. Total NPC."
"I'm not the main character today, I'm an NPC at the back of the class."
"Why does everyone in this town have NPC energy?"
"I walked past the same guy three times. NPC route."
"The cashier said 'have a nice day' like a dialogue box."

body: Calling yourself an NPC is self-deprecating and fine. Calling another person an NPC says they have no mind of their own, which is dismissive and can be hurtful, and online it is often used to brush off people with a different opinion. Use it about strangers' habits or yourself, not to win an argument.

faq.a: Non-player character, a game character controlled by the computer instead of a player.

faq.q: Is calling someone an NPC rude?
faq.a: Usually, yes. It implies they cannot think for themselves. Using it about yourself is just a joke.
